content: 1. Administer 1 mg/kg of intravenous medication daily for 4–5 months in cases of severe, widespread nodular cystic lesions that have not responded to oral antibiotic therapy. Alternative regimen 1: Doxycycline 100 mg orally twice daily. Alternative regimen 2: Minocycline 50 mg orally twice daily or Minocycline 1 mg/kg in an extended-release formulation once daily. Note: Other alternatives include tetracycline, erythromycin, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX), or clindamycin. 2. For acne rosacea: For facial erythema: Apply brimonidine gel topically twice daily to the affected area. For papulopustular rosacea: Preferred regimen 1: Azelaic acid gel applied topically twice daily. Preferred regimen 2: Metronidazole cream applied topically once daily. 3. For cutaneous anthrax: Preferred regimen 1: Penicillin V 500 mg orally four times daily for 7–10 days. Preferred regimen 2: Ciprofloxacin 500 mg orally twice daily. Preferred regimen 3: Levofloxacin 500 mg intravenously or orally once daily for 60 days in cases of bioterrorism due to presumed aerosol exposure. 4. For bacillary angiomatosis: Preferred regimen 1: Erythromycin 500 mg orally four times daily for 2 weeks to 2 months. Preferred regimen 2: Doxycycline 100 mg orally twice daily for 2 weeks to 2 months. In immunocompromised patients with relapse, continue retreatment for 4–6 months. Repeated relapses may require indefinite treatment. If Bartonella infections fail to respond to initial treatment, consider second-line regimens. 5. For Lyme disease: Adults: Preferred regimen 1: Amoxicillin 500 mg orally three times daily. Preferred regimen 2: Doxycycline 100 mg orally twice daily. Preferred regimen 3: Cefuroxime axetil 500 mg orally twice daily or 30 mg/kg/day orally twice daily (maximum 500 mg per dose). Preferred regimen 4: Ceftriaxone 2 g intravenously once daily. Alternative regimens: Doxycycline 200 mg orally as a single dose, Cefotaxime 2 g intravenously every 8 hours, or Penicillin G 18–24 million units/day intravenously every 4 hours. Pediatrics: Preferred regimen 1: Amoxicillin 50 mg/kg/day orally three times daily (maximum 500 mg per dose). Preferred regimen 2: For children aged ≥8 years, Doxycycline 4 mg/kg/day orally twice daily (maximum 100 mg per dose). Note: Doxycycline is not recommended for children under 8 years of age. 6. For bubonic plague: Preferred regimen 1: Streptomycin 15 mg/kg intramuscularly every 12 hours. Preferred regimen 2: Doxycycline 100 mg orally twice daily. Preferred regimen 3: Gentamicin may be substituted for streptomycin. 7. For carbuncles: Mild cases: Incision and drainage. Moderate cases: Empiric treatment with TMP-SMX or Doxycycline. MSSA (Methicillin-Susceptible Staphylococcus aureus): TMP-SMX. MRSA (Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus): Dicloxacillin or Cephalexin. Severe cases: Empiric treatment with Vancomycin, Daptomycin, Linezolid, Telavancin, or Ceftaroline. MSSA: Nafcillin, Cefazolin, or Clindamycin. MRSA: Vancomycin, Daptomycin, Linezolid, Telavancin, or Ceftaroline. 8. For cat scratch disease: In patients >45 kg: Azithromycin 500 mg orally on day 1, followed by 250 mg orally daily for 4 additional days. In patients <45 kg: Azithromycin 10 mg/kg orally on day 1, followed by 5 mg/kg orally daily for 4 additional days. 9. For cellulitis: Non-purulent cellulitis: Mild cases: Preferred regimen 1: Penicillin VK 500 mg orally twice daily. Preferred regimen 2: Cephalosporin. Preferred regimen 3: Dicloxacillin. Preferred regimen 4: Clindamycin 600–900 mg intravenously every 6–8 hours. Moderate cases: Preferred regimen 1: Penicillin VK 500 mg orally twice daily. Preferred regimen 2: Ceftriaxone 1–2 g every 4–8 hours. Preferred regimen 3: Cefazolin. Preferred regimen 4: Clindamycin 600–900 mg intravenously every 6–8 hours. Severe cases: Empiric treatment with Vancomycin and Piperacillin-Tazobactam. Purulent cellulitis: Mild cases: Incision and drainage. Moderate cases: Incision and drainage with empiric treatment using TMP-SMX or Doxycycline. MSSA: Dicloxacillin or Cephalexin. MRSA: TMP-SMX. Severe cases: Incision and drainage with empiric treatment using Vancomycin, Daptomycin, Linezolid, Telavancin, or Ceftaroline. 10. For erysipelas: Adults: Preferred regimen 1: Penicillin 500 mg orally four times daily. Preferred regimen 2: Amoxicillin 500 mg orally four times daily. Preferred regimen 3: Erythromycin 250 mg orally four times daily. Preferred regimen 4: Ceftriaxone 1 g intravenously once daily. Preferred regimen 5: Cefazolin 1–2 g intravenously every 8 hours. Pediatrics: Preferred regimen 1: Penicillin 25–50 mg/kg/day orally three to four times daily. Preferred regimen 2: Amoxicillin 25–50 mg/kg/day orally three times daily. Preferred regimen 3: Erythromycin 30–50 mg/kg/day orally two to four times daily. Preferred regimen 4: Ceftriaxone 50–75 mg/kg/day intravenously every 12–24 hours. Preferred regimen 5: Cefazolin 100 mg/kg/day intravenously every 8 hours. This is a partial response due to the extensive nature of the content.
